source: Quotes supplied by the project owner for ASG Eye Hospital and Renuka.
notes: Each figure is the price for the unit shown: per eye for one injection package, or per session for PRP laser.
The figures do not include consultation, OCT scans, or follow-up visits.
PRP laser usually needs more than one session, so the per-session price is not the total treatment cost.
Prices are hospital quotes and can change; confirm the current price and what it includes before treatment.

Intravitreal anti-VEGF injections are given into the eye by a retina specialist to reduce abnormal blood-vessel growth and fluid leakage in diabetic retinopathy, macular oedema and macular degeneration.
Panretinal photocoagulation (PRP) is laser treatment for abnormal new blood vessels, usually in severe or proliferative retinopathy.
A treatment is only used if the ophthalmologist finds disease that needs it. This screening tool cannot confirm that.

other_treatments.name: Focal or grid laser
other_treatments.summary: Targeted laser to leaking blood vessels away from the centre of the macula, used for localised swelling rather than the whole retina.

other_treatments.name: Intravitreal corticosteroid
other_treatments.purpose: macular oedema that does not settle
other_treatments.summary: A slow-release steroid implant or injection into the eye to reduce swelling. Your eye doctor will discuss the risks, including raised eye pressure and cataract.

other_treatments.name: Vitrectomy
other_treatments.summary: Surgery to remove blood or scar tissue from inside the eye when bleeding does not clear or the retina is being pulled away.

other_treatments.name: Control of glucose, blood pressure and cholesterol
other_treatments.summary: Keeping HbA1c, blood pressure and cholesterol in target supports every other treatment and lowers the chance of progression.
